title: Top Bun
format: Logo, paper bags, labels, shop sign, and van livery
summary: An identity a small bakery can afford to use every day. Made for a family bakery in Wigan, it works at four in the morning, on a paper bag, in floury hands.
coverAlt: Bread bags, a shop sign, and a delivery van in the Top Bun identity

blocks.heading: The idea
blocks.body: Bakers mark their loaves by hand with a single cut. I built the identity from that gesture. One scored line becomes the logo, the pattern on the bags, and the stripe on the van.

blocks.label: Research. Old bakery signs, bread scores, and paper bags from three local shops.

blocks.heading: Process
blocks.body: I tested the mark at the size of a price sticker first, because that is where most people meet it. Anything that failed there was cut. The type came last, a sturdy sans that survives a cheap printer and a greasy thumb.

blocks.caption: From sketches to the sticker test to the bag pattern.
The identity on bags, labels, and the shop sign.
The van stripe, the same scored line at full size.

blocks.heading: Reflection
blocks.body: The owner was often busy with a new invention, so the system had to run without me. Next time I would write the one-page guide first and design the identity to fit it.
